question: Which of the following sectors was the primary focus of India's First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture and Irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951–56)** in India was primarily focused on **Agriculture and Irrigation**. The main aim was to tackle food shortages and improve agricultural productivity in the newly independent country.
 
• India faced severe challenges such as **food insecurity, poor irrigation facilities, and low agricultural production** during the initial years of independence. Hence, agriculture was given top priority.
 
• The plan allocated around **44.6% of the total budget** to agriculture, irrigation, and community development projects, making it the largest share among all sectors.
 
• Key initiatives under the First Five-Year Plan included: **land reforms, irrigation projects, development of dams like Bhakra-Nangal and Hirakud, and community development programs** to empower rural areas.
 
• The plan aimed to achieve a **5% growth rate** in agriculture, which was considered a necessary step to ensure food security and support industrialization in the future.
 
• The focus on agriculture helped reduce dependency on food imports and laid the foundation for self-sufficiency in food production in subsequent years.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Agriculture and Irrigation.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the First Five-Year Plan:**

 
 
• The main goal was to **increase agricultural production** to tackle food shortages and improve the living standards of the rural population.
 
• The plan emphasized the development of **irrigation projects, rural infrastructure, and cooperative farming systems** to boost productivity.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the First Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• The plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar model**, which focused on investment and savings to drive economic growth.
 
• Major investments were made in **large-scale irrigation projects** such as Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud, and Damodar Valley projects to ensure reliable water supply for agriculture.
 
• **Community Development Programs** were launched to improve rural infrastructure, healthcare, education, and employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the First Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• The plan achieved a **3.6% annual growth rate**, which was close to its target of 5% growth.
 
• It helped India reduce dependency on **food imports** and laid the foundation for future economic development.
 
• The focus on **irrigation and agriculture** contributed significantly to rural development and poverty alleviation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Subsequent Plans:**

 
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–61) shifted focus to **industrialization**, unlike the First Plan, which prioritized agriculture.
 
• While the First Plan emphasized **, later plans aimed at diversifying the economy and promoting industrial and service sectors.
 
 
 
• Legacy of the First Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• The successful implementation of the plan demonstrated India’s capacity to address critical issues such as food shortages and rural development.
 
• It established the importance of agriculture in India’s economic planning and became the foundation for strategies in subsequent decades.
